"CRITICAL for Large Datasets (300K+ rows): Always map the Optional group by field when using slicer cards with large datasets. Without this mapping, the card downloads and processes ALL rows even if only a few unique values exist, causing severe performance issues and unresponsive dashboards. Map the same column from 'Items' (or appropriate dimension) to Optional group by to aggregate data before processing.
Example: A 'Brand' slicer with 10 unique values in a 334K row dataset will process only 10 values instead of 334K rows when Optional group by is used."
Pointed out by Engineering during DOMO-473323 (Jan 2026). This best practice resolved critical performance issues that nearly jeopardized a customer POC. Should be prominently highlighted to prevent similar issues.

Is there a way for Workbench to pull files based on a "contains" in the filename rather than the exact file name?

Instead of setting up a job (Configure, Source, Edit) with a file name at the end of the source edit path:
- Create a new directory to store the incoming file
- In the Workbench job setup (Configure tab)—>Source, Edit » Path to directory (with no filename)
- Set up the rest of the job normally and save

Whenever a file appears in your created directory, the WB will upload that file(and any other files that are in the directory).

Caution:
-The files that land in the directory MUST have IDENTICAL schema as the file uploaded before the new file.
- Need to build in Windows logic to delete the file after it is uploaded (maybe in Windows Task Scheduler), as only one file should reside in the directory at a time. For example, if you had two files in the directory and a third file appeared in the directory (all files having identical schemas), the workbench would upload all three files, which is why there can only be one file in the created directory at a time.

Here are the details for the Sub Flow Feature:

Sub-Flows Documentation
Overview
Sub-Flows enable you to call one workflow from within another, facilitating modular design and reuse of existing processes. This functionality helps teams build smarter, more efficient workflows by treating reusable sequences of steps as components that can pass data back to the parent workflow.


Configuring Workflow Outputs
When creating workflows intended to be used as Sub-Flows, you may want to define output parameters. Outputs allow the Sub-Flow to pass important values back to the parent workflow at runtime, where they can be referenced in subsequent steps. 


How to Add Outputs
1. In the workflow editor, locate the Variable List in the left panel.
2. Hover over the desired variable. A three-dot menu (...) will appear on the right side.
3. Click the three-dot menu and select Output from the options (Edit, Delete, Output).
4. The selected variable will now be designated as an output and will appear in the Outputs section.

You can add multiple outputs of any variable type. 
How to Remove Outputs
* In the Outputs section, hover over the output variable you want to remove.
* Click the trash can icon that appears to delete the output.


Using Sub-Flows
Sub-Flows allow you to integrate one existing workflow into another and access its results, enabling complex automation with reusable components.

Adding a Sub-Flow to Your Workflow
1. Add or edit a step in the workflow canvas.
2. Open the Action Menu and select the Sub-Flows option.
3. In the configuration panel, click the Add Sub-Flow button.
4. The Sub-Flow Selection modal will open.
5. Search or scroll through the dropdown list, which shows only deployed Sub-Flows accessible to you.
6. Select the desired workflow.
    * Details including description, creator, inputs, outputs, and workflow design preview will be displayed.
7. Click Add Sub-Flow to confirm your selection.

Managing Assigned Sub-Flows
Once a Sub-Flow is assigned, you can:

* Change the selected Sub-Flow
* View details
* Remove the Sub-Flow
* Test run the Sub-Flow

These options are accessible by clicking the three-dot menu (...) on the Sub-Flow designation tile in the configuration panel.


Sub-Flow Execution Modes
Within the sub-flow configuration panel, you will find two execution mode options (presented as radio buttons): You can choose how the Sub-Flow behaves when your main workflow reaches that step:

* Run and Wait (default): The parent workflow pauses execution until the Sub-Flow completes, allowing any output variables to be received and used in subsequent steps.
* Run and Continue: The parent workflow initiates the Sub-Flow and immediately proceeds to the next step without waiting for Sub-Flow completion. Outputs are not captured in this mode.

Choose the mode based on whether you need to wait for Sub-Flow results before continuing.


Mapping Inputs and Outputs
Inputs
* Map inputs required by the Sub-Flow to variables or custom values in the parent workflow.
* Input types must match or be compatible with the Sub-Flow’s input parameters.

Outputs
* Map output variables from the Sub-Flow to variables within the parent workflow to capture results.
* If necessary, create new variables in the parent workflow to receive mapped outputs.


Sub-Flow Meta Data (Optional)
At the bottom of the Sub-Flow configuration panel is the Sub-Flow Meta Data section.

* This section allows you to map variables to optional metadata about the Sub-Flow execution.
* These parameters are not required and can be left unassigned if you do not need the metadata.


Summary
By utilizing Sub-Flows, you can build workflows that are both modular and maintainable, promote reuse of common processes, and manage data exchange between nested workflows through defined inputs and outputs.

The Domo Stats for Task Center introduces a new connector option that allows customers to create a DataSet for their task usage. Each row in the dataset represents a task and will include relevant details about the task, such as when it was created, the status, if/when it was completed, who completed, and much more.   This feature enables users to query and analyze their task usage data, as well as design cards, dashboards, reports, and other visualizations to uncover deeper insights. 

A new report name and description needs to be added to the page for Task Center.  

The schema for the new dataset will contain the follow datapoints:

Task ID - the unique identification number for the task
Task Identifier - field value(s) that have been configured as task identifier
Form Name - The name of the form being used in the task
Form ID - the unique ID of the form  
Task Status - the status of the task
Queue - the name of the queue where the task is located
Queue ID - the unique ID of the queue
Created On - the date the task was created
Completed On - the date the task was completed
Completed By - the ID of the person that completed the task
Assignee - the ID of the person or group that is assigned to the task
Assignee Type - the type of assignee assigned to the task (either User or Group)
Source ID - the ID of the source that generated the task
Source Entity - the entity type of the source that generated task (e.g. Workflow)
Updated On - the date the latest update occurred on the task

All existing permission controls for DomoStats still apply.

Provide a detailed explanation of what needs to be created/updated:
This features adds new screens and capabilities to the Workflow tool that enable better visibility into the different mechanisms configured to start a specific workflow version and the ability to navigate to those triggering entities to change or remove the integration.   

All triggers that started a workflow existed before this feature, but now any trigger that is integrated and configured to start a specific workflow version will now be visible so users know all the ways that version can be initiated.   In addition, users have the ability to navigate to the entity where the trigger can be set up from the workflow.   In some cases, certain triggers can be set up in the workflow tool.  

With the exception of a manual trigger, all other triggers can only be set up on a workflow after the workflow has been deployed.  This includes Timers.   Before, timer starts could be set up in the canvas as the workflow was being built, but with the implementation of this feature, timer starts can only be configured after the workflow has been deployed.  

If a user wants to add a trigger, they can select the add trigger button either in the new trigger panel in the canvas or in the new trigger tab in version page.  When they select a trigger type, a modal will pop up telling them how to add the trigger.  (Again, they could always add these triggers before, but now we help them navigate to the entity to set up or let them do it directly in the tool, depending on the type of trigger. 

Trigger types include: 
Manual - every workflow is automatically configured with a manual trigger.  Users can click the start button after a workflow has been deployed to manually initiative an execution of that workflow version.  There is no process the user needs to complete to set up a manual trigger.

Alert - To add an alert trigger, navigate to the DataSet page and select the desired dataset. Select the Alerts tab and create a new alert or choose an existing one. Set up the alert using the configuration modal. For the Action, choose the Workflow version you want to start when the alert is triggered. 

App Studio - To create an App Studio trigger, navigate to the app you want to use in App Studio. Select the option to edit the app, then add the workflow widget component and assign it to the appropriate workflow version. Once configured, the App Studio trigger will appear in your trigger list for the corresponding workflow.

API - An API Trigger can be added form the workflow tool.  However, there is syntax generated (that contains a trigger ID) when the trigger is added for the customer to copy and paste into the the API call. Any calls made with this trigger ID will be used exclusively for tracking purposes, allowing the customer to identify which trigger initiated your workflow.

Pro-Code App - To create a Pro-Code app trigger, you can either select an existing app design from the Asset Library that’s already configured with a workflow and map it to a card, or choose the "Pro-Code Editor" option to build a new Pro-Code app. You can program the app design to use a workflow, which can then be selected and mapped via the card configuration panel.

Timer -  Lets the user set up an interval to start the Workflow.  They can configure the timer start directly in the tool after the workflow has been deployed.  

Workflow - A workflow trigger is used when you want one workflow to initiate another. To create a workflow trigger, navigate to the workflow you want to use as the triggering workflow, then add a step to start another workflow. To do this, search for "Start Workflow" in the top-level search bar in the action menu and select the Start Workflow package. Next, locate the desired workflow in the function list and map the necessary parameters. Once the triggering workflow is deployed, it will appear on the trigger list for the selected workflow.  


After a trigger is added it is visible either from the new trigger panel in the canvas or the workflow version page.   

To access the trigger panel in the canvas, click on the Start icon in the left  gallery.  This will show any configured triggers set up to start that specific version.  If you click on the start icon before the workflow has been deployed, it will display a message that the workflow has not been deployed and no triggers can be set up yet.  

The version page has been updated to be a three tabbed screen .  The Versions tab shows the Version list for the Workflow and functions the same way as it does today.  The Triggers tab shows all the configured triggers for each version in the workflow.  From this tab, users can navigate to the entity where the trigger has been set up to change or remove it.   The Executions tab shows all the initiated executions for the workflow and works in the same manner as it does today.  All three tabs are accessible from the same page.  


Triggers for Alerts,App Studio,  Pro-code App, and Workflows can be deleted by navigating to the entity where it was set up and removing it.  Triggers for Timers and APIs can be deleted by clicking the delete icon on their configuration modals.

We have updated the limit for Pivot Tables a bit. There is a section in this article 'Best Practices for Pivot Tables' where it mentions 10 as the max number of combinations. We've updated how this limit is defined: It is now a limit for the number of queries that need to be called, and the max number of queries is 36. The formula to get to this limit is:

(NumberOfRowPills + 1) x (NumberOfColumnPills + 1) <=36

For example, a Pivot with 8 row pills and 1 column pill would require 18 queries to render:

8 rows x 1 columns => (8+1) x (1+1) => 9 x 2 = 18 queries

There are a lot more possible combinations now, but here are some possible combinations

1 x 17
2 x 11
3 x 8
4 x 6
5 x 5
6 x 4
8 x 3
11 x 2
17 x 1

There are several things that need adjusted.
The new Macros will apply to dates in Mega Tables and Pivot tables in addition to the other charts
h and hh are 12 hour times. A single h will only display 1 digit unless the hour is 10, 11 or 12, while the hh will display hours like 05
H and HH work exactly the same as h and hh except the time is in 24 hour
For day of the week it should be EEE for a 3 digit day of week, while EEEE will output the complete day of week name. (We made a code change so E, EE and EEE all do the same thing 3 digit day name)
d and D and dd and DD are the same. Like hours a single d or D will not put 0’s before single digit days, while dd and DD always output 2 digits
MMM outputs a 3 letter Month abbreviation, MMMM or MMMMM outputs the full month name
there are several shortcuts for international dates : L, LL, LLL, LLL, LT, LTS. The order of days, months, years, etc will depend on the locale.
As an example for US English, they would be as follows:
        LT, "h:mm a"
        LTS, "h:mm:ss a"
        L, "MM/dd/yyyy"
        LL, "MMMMM d, yyyy"
        LLL, "MMMMM d, yyyy h:mm a"
        LLLL, "EEEE, MMMMM d, yyyy h:mm a

New article to cover our support of SCIM, which is the System for Cross-domain Identity Management. This is a new API we're supporting. It doesn't current have a front-end within the app, but is definitely an admin function, so the article should be somewhere in Admin. At the moment, we only support managing users, but will eventually allow group mgmt as well. The target for this article is a technical customer admin.

---

Intro
The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is a standard that defines API endpoints that systems can use to manage identity. In the context of Domo, SCIM can be used to manage users. For example, you can use Okta to manage your Domo users via SCIM.

For more details on SCIM, please see this article: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644

Requirements
To use the SCIM endpoints, you will need to create an [access token|https://domohelp.domo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042934494-Managing-Access-Tokens]. This token must be associated to a user with the "Add People" and/or "Manage all Users" grants, based on the actions you'd like to take.

Supported Actions
We support the following SCIM endpoints and verbs. For details of what is required with each action, please refer to the SCIM spec: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644

> GET /api/identity/v1/scim/ServiceProviderConfig
> GET api/identity/v1/scim/Schemas/User
> GET api/identity/v1/scim/Users/{userId}
> PUT api/identity/v1/scim/Users/{userId}
> DELETE api/identity/v1/scim/Users/{userId}
> POST api/identity/v1/scim/Users 
> GET api/identity/v1/scim/Users *This follows the SCIM search spec: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644#section-3.4.2.2

Example

FAQ Question:
Can I use Beast Mode calculations in DDX Bricks?

FAQ Answer:
Yes, you can use Beast mode calculations in DDX cards.

Here are a couple of things to remember:

1. The Beast Mode must be saved to the DataSet.

2. The query must include the parameter "useBeastMode=true"

3. When you refer a Beast Mode calculation in the query, refer it by its ID in the data query. If the beast mode is aliased, you can refer it by its alias in the query in the in the returned result set.

4. Beast Mode aliases can be found using the Beast Mode report in the Domo Governance connector.

5. If the Beast Mode calculation is aggregated then the aggregation statement can be left out of the query. 

6. If the Beast Mode is not aggregated, the aggregation statement must be included in the query.

In Magic ETL's R and Python scripting environment, you can use two special directories to store and share data between scripting tiles in a DataFlow. These directories are the "project" directory and the "/tmp" directory.
/tmp directory: The /tmp directory is a shared space for all scripting tiles within a DataFlow. If you create a file in the /tmp directory in one scripting tile, you can access it from another scripting tile within the same DataFlow. Keep in mind that the contents of the /tmp directory are temporary and will be deleted between executions.

Examples of using /tmp directory:
1.	Create multiple output dataframes in one script as files in /tmp and use them in separate tables in downstream scripting tiles.
2.	Share an object between scripting tiles that can't be easily represented as a dataframe.
3.	Improve communication efficiency between scripting tiles.

How to set up /tmp directory
1.	Create your DataFlow with the necessary scripting tiles (Python and/or R) and any required input and output DataSet tiles.
2.	In the first scripting tile (Python and/or R), write your script to process the data as needed and save the resulting data or objects to the /tmp directory. For example:
3.	In the second scripting tile (Python and/or R), read the data saved in the /tmp directory from the previous tile:
4.	Continue processing the data as needed, and use the output DataSet tile to save the final results.


Project directory: The "project" directory is another shared space for all scripting tiles within a DataFlow, but unlike the /tmp directory, its contents persist between executions. This means that you can store things like statistical models in the project directory and continue working on them across multiple executions. The project directory is located at /home/domo/project, but you can simply refer to it as "project" in your script. Note that any changes you make to the project directory are only saved after successful executions. Changes from preview or failed executions are discarded.
The total size of a project directory may not exceed 8 GiB. Contact Domo Support if you need to increase this limit, restore a directory from a backup, or copy a directory from one DataFlow to another.
Examples of using the project directory:
1.	Train a statistical model over time, allowing you to keep multiple versions while you figure out which one works best.
2.	Update complex calculations or aggregate statistics with new data instead of re-computing everything from scratch, when used with the Input DataSet option that loads only new batches since the last successful execution.

How to set up project directory: 
1.	Create your DataFlow with the necessary scripting tiles (Python and/or R) and any required input and output DataSet tiles.
2.	In the first scripting tile (e.g., Python or R), write your script to process the data incrementally and save the intermediate results or models to the project directory. For example:
 3.	In another scripting tile (e.g., Python or R), read the intermediate results or models saved in the project directory from the previous tile and continue processing as needed:
4.	Save the final results or updated models back to the project directory, if needed, and use the output DataSet tile to store the final results.

These two directories provide useful ways to store and share data within your Magic ETL scripting environment, making it easier to work with complex data processing tasks.

Sydney Trains would like this detail added so there’s no confusion around the varying column numbers / differing column datatypes. Their testing (attached) has confirmed that the schema is being preserved by the ServiceNow upsert connector as explained by Support. 

- Domo preserves old schemas.  This is done in case someone makes a mistake and the returning schema is completely different from initial ones, which would break all assets using the old schema.  
- If a query does not return a field that was previously populated, the field in the dataset will be blanked out but won’t be deleted.
- Domo tries to infer the data type of a column when it ingests it. We could tell the connector to not change datatypes but in the case of a custom query where we don’t have insight into the fields before they come over, it would not be advisable.  E.g., suppose the connector initially infers that column is a numeric because that’s what coming in during the first run.  If on the next run, the query returns something with a character and a numeric, then the connector will fail because it will recognize the column as String instead of numeric.
- The connector will ingest the fields the API sends over. So if the API doesn’t send over a field, the connector can’t ingest it.

NOTE: When adding Graphics, Links, and Images to Table Cards using Beast Mode,

Regardless of who requests the access, these rules still apply.

Note, this is a very high security/high consequence action. Please be 100% sure you’ve triple checked everything and watch for the signs of social engineering. You and Domo can be liable for missteps in this regard. When in doubt, ask one of your senior colleagues or a manager.

3.	Written authorization (email from client with matching domain name), and job title of Director, VP, Executive will be acceptable. If this is a marketing use case, we would want someone at the VP level of their marketing team indicating their approval. If it is the VP itself asking for this admin access, then we would go to their boss, etc. This individual would preferably someone whose name appears on the contract/oppty/onboarding documents. Once approved in writing, support will make notes on the case and take appropriate action to grant access.

In the event none of these methods are possible, then alert your manager and accounts team that it may need escalation.

Provide a detailed explanation of what needs to be created/updated:
I am actually not sure which article would be better, but our map charts will try to select the best map based on the data first entered into the chart building process. We received the following information from an engineering ticket (DOMO-347144):

The US map is unique in that it really could be one of several different maps. The actual map loaded is inferred from the column name / alias (Data Label) of the first column.

We first look to see if the column name includes "zip", if so we try to use the zipcode level map of the US.

If it doesn't include "zip" then we look for "fip" or "county" in the column name, and if either of those are present we load the county level map of the US. We then do the same tests for the alias or "Data Label" for the column.

Finally if the column name includes "st" short for "state" then we load the state level map.

So in this case, because they have set the column name in the ETL to be "zip2fip"... it picks up on that column name and determines the map to use should be the zipcode level map.

We should add this information to the KB so that customer's are aware of this quirk in how maps try to render the data.

Provide a detailed explanation of what needs to be created/updated:
Passing data into apps via URL parameters
 
Non-sensitive data can be passed into apps through a couple main types of parameters. The first is called “pfilters” and is already very popular because it has been available for years. Examples are documented in
https://domohelp.domo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042933114-Using-Pfilters-to-Apply-Filters-from-URL-Query-Parameters-to-Embedded-Dashboards .
 
The second is called “appData” and is much newer. It supports passing in more general types of data to the app. The app developer needs to watch for the parameter, parse the value, and inject it into the most relevant part of the app.
 
If an app developer was less concerned about the column, operand, and value of pfilters, this general parameter could be appended to the embed URL. For example, the value of the parameter could then auto-populate a drop-down menu in an app that selects the location. This way, the host page can avoid the delay of waiting for manual inputs. They can now deep-link to a version of the app that already has specific values filled in. Spaces should be encoded as “+” :
 
public.domo.com/embed/pages/abcde?appData=Salt+Lake+City
 
Both parameter types could also be combined in this way:
 
public.domo.com/embed/pages/abcde
?appData=Salt+Lake+City
&pfilters=[
{
"column":"Role",
"operand":"IN",
"values":["Director","Manager"],
},
{
"column":"Team",
"operand":"IN",
"values":["Sales","Marketing"],
}
]
 
The query parameters on the embed URL will then be automatically passed down into the apps (e.g. xyz.domoapps.prod4.domo.com) contained by the embedded cards or dashboards. Again, the main part that is not automatic is the manual work for the developer to code the app in a way that injects that parameter value in field that should be pre-populated.

I love the updates you put in for the SharePoint Online Rest connector, I have had a lot of calls for that connector recently and the updates have helped out a ton! Microsoft App Steps:
A lot of customers are getting stuck between permissions (step 10), and setting up the Domo connector.  After adding the permissions, their Admin (or possibly their SuperAdmin if they have one) will need to grant the Microsoft Azure portal app those permissions.  The screen shot below shows how it looks before granting.   You can see the “Grant admin consent for Domo Inc.” is grayed out for me because I am not a Microsoft Azure admin, but if I was, the next step would be to check that box to grant access.  Once granted the “Status” section turns green like the screen shot on the KB article.  The attached image is an unedited version of the screen shot for the KB.

 
 
Domo SharePoint Online Rest Connector Steps/Troubleshooting:
The next couple of issues are pretty common as well and I think if we add some notes or a FAQs to the bottom, it could really be useful. 
 
Issue:
Unable to authenticate to Microsoft through the Domo SharePoint Online Rest connector.
 
What to Check:
Browser cookie/cache issues.  
When the users is signed into any Microsoft sites and attempts to sign in to the Domo SharePoint Online Rest connector with the account used on the Azure portal, a browser conflict can occur that prevents the Domo user from authenticating to Microsoft.  Normally a small Oauth pop up window appears.  When this issue happens, the pop up window might not appear, or it might flash open and disappears(most common), and sometimes the window appears and provides an error message. 
 
What to Check:
Before signing using the Domo connector, sign out and close all internet browser based Microsoft products.  On occasion, this still fails to load the pop up authentication window.  If this happens, close all browser windows and attempt signing into the Domo SharePoint Online Rest connector in an incognito window. 
 
Issue:
Able to authenticate to SharePoint Online Rest connector, but has partial access or no access to data.

(Current)
--------------------------------
Returns the string that results from concatenating the arguments, separated by the separator, for the whole group. May have one or more arguments, plus the optional separator. If not set, the separator is the comma character '',''. All arguments are converted to strings.

 It is an aggregate function.

(After)
--------------------------------
Returns the string that results from concatenating the arguments, separated by the separator, for the whole group. May have one or more arguments, plus the optional separator. If not set, the separator is the comma character '',''. All arguments are converted to strings.

 It is an aggregate function.

GROUP_CONCAT() returns null if there were no matching rows.

NOTE: The GROUP_CONCAT function does not support “ORDER BY” or "DISTINCT" as part of the expression in the New Magic ETL.
--------------------------------



Justification:
Please see the comments of https://onjira.domo.com/browse/DOMO-340275.
--------------------------------
 The GROUP_CONCAT function does not support “ORDER BY” or "DISTINCT" as part of the expression in Magic ETL. Those options are presently accomplishable in MySQL and Domo's Adrenaline DataFlow (premium feature). We intend to add support for those functions in a future release.

In the meantime, it is possible to produce the desired result by using a combination of other Magic ETL tiles. Rank & Window can provide the ORDER BY, and Remove Duplicates can provide the DISTINCT. Insert these tiles before the group by, and for the sort/distinct key provide the columns of the grouping key followed by the string to be concatenated. If more than one GROUP_CONCAT is needed, use multiple such tile chains followed by joins to combine their results.
--------------------------------

I would like to add a note at the top of this KB article about an additional troubleshooting step to take in the case that the Domo Connector Package has been installed for all users in Salesforce but some users are still unable to access the Salesforce connector. 

If the Domo Connector Package has been installed for all users but some users are getting the following error message: 
"Domo is ready, but you have not installed Salesforce's Domo Connector Package. For help, refer to instructions at https://knowledge.domo.com?cid=sfmanagedpackage."

Please suggest the following:
Sometimes a Salesforce profile (profiles in Salesforce are similar to groups) will get set up after the Domo Connector Package has been installed. This can cause the profile to not get fully set up with the Domo Connector Package even if it gets installed for all users again. In the case that this happens, the client's Salesforce admin will want to go into the user's profile and look for the Apex Class List permission. Once in there, they can search for the two DomoReporting apps and add them to the Apex Class List. Once this has been saved, those users should be able to use the Salesforce Connector in Domo.

Q: What is the timeout for loading data from Snowflake?
A:

Viewing data on-screen and exporting data are subject to different timeouts within Domo. These timeouts only apply to the Domo side of the action and are not issued to Snowflake. However, Domo does respect the Snowflake session timeout.

Examples:
> If a card cannot be rendered within the Domo timeout, an error message is displayed on-screen, but the Snowflake query is not cancelled. That query is then subject to the timeout defined in Snowflake.
> If a card cannot be rendered within the Snowflake timeout, and that timeout is less than the Domo timeout, an error message is displayed on-screen and the query is cancelled (from the Snowflake side).

Timeouts:
> Cards will attempt to render on-screen for up to 1-minute.
> Exports, both from cards and datasets, will attempt to export for up to 12-hours.

To change the Snowflake session timeout, adjust the STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS session parameter. We recommend adjusting this setting based on the primary usage of your datasets. For example, if they're primarily used for exporting, you may want a longer timeout than if the datasets are primarily being used to render cards in Domo.

Please add new FAQs:

- How does caching work?
Results are cached at a DataSet & SQL query level. Every card, custom app and Data Flow produce SQL used to select results from an underlying DataSet. It's that combination of the produced SQL and the DataSet that serves as a cache key. If multiple cards produce the same SQL to retrieve data from the same DataSet, they may utilize the same cache. The same goes for multiple users that access a card or cards producing the same SQL against the same DataSet.

- How is caching impacted by filtering and/or PDP?
Filtering (page filters, card filters, filter views, etc) and PDP are included in the underlying SQL. This means that a given card may have multiple cache keys as described in the above FAQ, particularly if each user has different PDP rules.

- When does a cache expire?
The cache timeout (TTL - time to live) is set on the adapter by the user configuring the connection.

Name: JavaScript vs iframe in Embed
Notes:
From: Chris Haleua (7/21/21)

This is a long shot, but if you magically have some time to turn this internal POV into an external KB article, I would be happy to meet anytime to work on a draft together:
 
We got a question about JS vs iframe after the call. Here is how I usually respond to iframe worries:

JS vs iframe is a fair concern. Nevertheless, we have been able to overcome it with clients of all sizes.

Over the years, the main reasons some embed customers have asked for JS embed instead of iframes have been:
· Customizing the appearance
· Adapting responsively across device types
· Loading quickly across regions
· Maintaining compatibility across browsers

Those have been our main guiding principles as we have expanding beyond card embed to dashboard embed. The appearance can be customized through the custom layouts, background colors, images, and fonts that customers has already used to push the capabilities of Publish to new heights. Fortunately, Embed already had quite a head start here since it has a more direct path to inheriting the experience directly from the instance where it was created. You can see that continuing to develop as we add page filters and page exports.

Responsive design started as a quick test for a prospect that wanted to embed dashboards in the Salesforce mobile app. Only a month after we built it, the functionality was really put to the test with the Domo Covid Tracker. 65% of our traffic there was on mobile. It pushed us to move beyond dynamically reformatting the layout to a vertical stack of cards. Mobile layout edit capabilities will be released very soon. We also added a way to dynamically resize the iframe with postmessage to avoid scroll traps. Now embed works reliably on large screens, mobile browsers, and dedicated mobile apps.

Visualization flexibility is higher than ever with DDX apps. For the few chart types that Domo does not already support, JavaScript can be simply pasted in-line and details can be edited in the context of the greater layout to avoid totally building everything from scratch. 

Loading quickly becomes an even greater priority when the lag between the host page loading and the embedded content loading becomes the focus of the viewer’s attention. For that reason, we have been obsessing over speed for the past few months. This has led to a variety of improvements with iframe speed. We started with gzip compression to make the assets as small as possible. Then we continued by reducing the size of the JS that drives the iframe even before compression. Then we changed to activate browser caching by default. Then we consolidated API calls to avoid duplicate requests when validating columns. Finally, we are in the process of releasing CDN integration so that the cache can be stored closer to our international customers. All these things result in iframe load times that are significantly faster than they were last year.

Compatibility across browsers is the final hurdle. This is definitely one to watch as we move from third party cookies to header-based authentication. For now, Safari is the most strict. They have already started to block 3rdparty cookies. Chrome will follow in the next couple years as Google figures out how to make their ad tracking work without it. In the meantime, it only really impacts Domo embed in a small segment: app embed on Safari. For that we already have a workaround. The user clicks an “accept cookies” button similar to the GDPR dialogs that are common on almost every website these days. Fortunately, card and dashboard embed (especially when programmatically filtered through the JWT) do not have even have to show the “accept cookies” button because the token is based on header auth.

We use JS where it is essential (authentication and context). For authentication, we use JS to drive the server-side personalization at the row level. We recently expanded upon that to even switch datasets dynamically. For context, we use JS to push filters down from the host page into the embedded content. Then we also use that same message channel to pull click events from the embedded content back to the host page. That is very helpful in linking across pages with and without embedded content. 

After that, the only reason to use JS for embed is to define the actual experience. That is where you must make a decision. Do you want the experience to only be editable by those comfortable with coding JS or for everyone familiar with the drag and drop experience of story layouts? Do you want the updates to be reliant on the release schedule for the web development team or do you need the edits to be immediately applied as soon as someone presses the save button in Domo? It is true that stories needs to continue progressing, but I am quite confident that we can help customers move faster than you could if you had to rebuild all the interactions from scratch in JS.

If your team has other iframe concerns, I would be happy to discuss this further.
 
 
-CH

Users who have previously created documents with Domo Content via the legacy plugins now are able to convert that document to the new Addins.

1. From my tests, it appears as though the closing exclamation mark (!) is required, but the examples are inconsistent.
 
2. It is not made clear in the documentation that the "lastrundate" tag is replaced by a single-quoted string.  For example:
 
Input:
!{lastrundate:start_date}!
Output:
'1700-02-01 07:05:11'
 
3. The documentation shows "lastrundate" as a "MM/dd/yyyy" format string, but in my tests, it is replaced by a "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" format string.  BigQuery requires the string to be cast to a DATE or DATETIME type.  In this example, it's being cast first to a DATETIME and then to a DATE:
 
WHERE start_date >= CAST(
  CAST(
    !{lastrundate:start_date}!
    AS DATETIME FORMAT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'
  )
  AS DATE
)
 
4. The Query section shows "lastValue:id" but the Query Parameters section shows "lastValue:_id" (note the underscore).
 
5. My tests show that "lastValue" should be "lastvalue" (all lowercase).

Under Brand Kit settings, we are adding an enhancement to allow customers to send Domo generated emails through their own email server. This specific enhancement allows customers to modify the "From" address in Domo generated emails and specify the name and email address that these emails are sent from.

This affects all emails generated by an event in Domo, except for emails that revolve around logging into Domo (ie Password reset, You've been Domo'd, etc.) and any emails that allow you to invite people to join Domo (ie Card shares).

But for emails like Scheduled Reports or Alerts, they will come from the customer's email domain.

Domo whitelists the email servers that are compatible. If a customer wishes to use a server that currently isn't whitelisted, they should contact their CSM to request it.

When customers add a server, they will be required to enter in their login credentials to their server. They will then need to verify this connection. Once verified, they can choose to use the email server or still rely on Domo's server.

Customers may add as many email servers as they want, but they can only choose to use one at a time.

This also supports customers adding headers to their emails if they want to track them.
